kinds.name: acp_harness
kinds.doc:
Drives an Agent Client Protocol agent, and serves it as one ACP connection over a channel.

The host is the ACP client and the provider the agent: each message on the channel, either way,
is one whole JSON-RPC 2.0 message as UTF-8 JSON text. The kind never models ACP itself, so a
provider in any language implements ACP as the protocol defines it, and the version is agreed by
`initialize` on the channel.

Every method is synchronous; a host calls them from a thread of its own.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
Who the harness is and what its `initialize` will advertise, with nothing started: for a host
listing its harnesses. Cheap, and the same on every call.

slots.name: start
slots.doc:
Starts one ACP connection: messages the host sends are the client's, and the agent's come back
through `sink`.

The sink is handed over: the provider destroys it, even when it refuses. It returns once the
channel takes messages; the program it drives may start later, at `initialize` or
`session/new`, and a failure then is answered in ACP before the provider closes.

It refuses with `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` when it would refuse any of the request's
requirements ([`refusal`](Self::refusal)), and with `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` a request it cannot
read; it never starts with a requirement left out.

slots.name: refusal
slots.doc:
Why the harness could not hold a connection to `requirement`, started with `environment`, in a
sentence; `None` when it can. A host asks before it starts one, and passes over a harness
that would refuse. The default refuses every requirement, known or not.

slots.name: models
slots.doc:
The models the account behind `environment` may use, when the harness can say without a model
turn. Never carries a value from `environment`. The default: unknown, and says so.

slots.name: program
slots.doc:
The program the harness starts, a name looked up on `PATH` or a path, so a host can say it
cannot be found before it starts a connection. The default: `None`, and the host does not look.

slots.name: session_record
slots.doc:
Where the harness keeps its own record of the session `query` names, when it keeps one and the
file is there. The default: none.

kinds.name: channel
kinds.doc:
What the host writes on, handed back by the provider that started it.

The provider implements it and the host holds the channel object,
which may be shared between threads: `send` may be called from several
at once, each thread's messages kept in its own order. Dropping the
channel is `close(GUATIAO_OK)`.

slots.name: send
slots.doc:
One message to the provider, lent for the call. Returns once the
provider has taken it, which may wait on the provider; answers
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` once either side has closed, and a `send` that
was waiting when the host closed answers it too.

slots.name: close
slots.doc:
Ends the stream from the host's side, with a `guatiao_status` the
provider hands to the sink's `closed`: `GUATIAO_OK` (0) for a plain
end, an error status otherwise. Called once, and returns without
waiting for a `receive` still running; `send` answers
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` after it. Cannot fail.

kinds.name: channel_sink
kinds.doc:
What the provider writes back on, handed in by the host.

The host implements it and hands it over with the call that starts
the channel; the provider owns it from then on, makes every call on it
from one thread at a time, and destroys it when done.

slots.name: receive
slots.doc:
One message to the host, lent for the call. Returns once the host
has taken it, and a host never waits in it for its own `send`.
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` says the host takes nothing more; any error
ends the stream, and the provider then calls `closed` with that
status and delivers nothing still queued.

slots.name: closed
slots.doc:
The stream has ended, from either side: with the host's status from
the channel's `close`, or the provider's own, a `guatiao_status`
(`GUATIAO_OK` is the normal end). Called exactly once, and nothing
but `destroy` follows it. Cannot fail.
